plain: A Social Security rule that keeps MO HealthNet for some SSI workers whose pay ends the SSI check.
pro: Section 1619(b) Medicaid continuation; Missouri threshold 2026 $55,181 a year (POMS SI 02302.200).

plain: Missouri uses its own Medicaid rules. SSI does not bring MO HealthNet by itself. You must apply to FSD.
pro: State that uses eligibility criteria more restrictive than SSI under Section 1902(f); Missouri confirmed (POMS SI 01715.010).

plain: A school plan for supports under Section 504, for a student who does not need special education.
pro: Accommodation plan under Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act.

plain: Augmentative and alternative communication: tools that help a person communicate without speech, such as a speech device.
National groups of doctors for children, family medicine, and internal medicine.
pro: American Academy of Pediatrics, American Academy of Family Physicians, American College of Physicians.

plain: Applied behavior analysis, a therapy often used for autism.
A savings account for a person whose disability began before 46. It does not count against SSI up to $100,000.
pro: Account under 26 USC 529A; onset before 46 from 1 Jan 2026.

plain: A letter from FSD that says what it decided. Appeal deadlines count from the date on it.
pro: FSD notice of action; hearing due within 90 days of its date, 10 days to keep benefits.

plain: The Americans with Disabilities Act. A federal law against unfair treatment because of disability.
pro: Americans with Disabilities Act; Title II covers state and local government.

plain: MO HealthNet for adults 19 to 64 with low income and no Medicare.
pro: Medicaid expansion group, ME code E2; MAGI at or under 138% FPL.

plain: Administrative law judge. A judge who hears Social Security appeals.
Advanced practice registered nurse, a nurse who can diagnose and prescribe.
Autism spectrum disorder.
Health terms. BMI is body mass index. COPD is a lung disease. GERD is acid reflux.
pro: Body mass index; chronic obstructive pulmonary disease; gastroesophageal reflux disease.

plain: Missouri monthly cash and MO HealthNet for some blind adults who cannot get SSI.
pro: Missouri Blind Pension; grant $949 a month (Appendix K 07/2026).

plain: Benefits Planning Query. A Social Security report that lists a person's benefits.
Bureau of Special Health Care Needs. It runs the adult nursing waiver.
pro: DHSS Bureau of Special Health Care Needs; (800) 451-0669.

plain: Blind work expenses. Work costs that Social Security subtracts from a blind person's pay.
Client Assistance Program. Free help with problems in VR or RSB job services.
pro: Client Assistance Program at Mo P&A, 1-800-392-8667.

plain: Childhood Disability Benefits. Social Security pays an adult disabled before 22 from a parent's record.
pro: Childhood Disability Benefits, also Disabled Adult Child (DAC) benefits.

plain: Consumer-directed services. The person hires and directs their own home care worker.
Code of Federal Regulations. The book of federal rules.
The federal agency that runs Medicare and Medicaid.
pro: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services.

plain: A person a court picks to manage another adult's money and property.
A local helper for DD-eligible people without MO HealthNet in some counties.
pro: DDD Provider Resource and Referral (DDD Division Services sheet, 2024).

plain: Consumer Price Index. A measure of rising prices used to raise some limits each year.
pro: Consumer Price Index (RSMo 208.010 resource limit increases).

plain: Code of State Regulations. The book of Missouri agency rules.
City Utilities of Springfield. It runs the city bus and Access Express.
pro: City Utilities of Springfield, Transit Services.

plain: Disabled Adult Child. Another name for CDB. DAC rules can protect MO HealthNet when CDB ends SSI.
pro: Disabled Adult Child; Section 1634(c) Medicaid protection (POMS SI 01715.015).

plain: Disability Benefits 101, an online tool about work and benefits.
pro: Disability Benefits 101, funded in part by MODDC.

plain: Developmental disability. A disability that starts before 22 and lasts for life, such as autism or cerebral palsy.
pro: Developmental disability as defined in RSMo 630.005.

plain: The DMH Division of Developmental Disabilities. It runs DD eligibility, support coordination, and DD waivers.
The Missouri education department. It oversees special education and Missouri VR.
pro: Department of Elementary and Secondary Education.

plain: The Missouri health department. It runs in-home care for adults.
pro: Department of Health and Senior Services.

plain: The Missouri Department of Mental Health. It includes the Division of Developmental Disabilities.
The U.S. Department of Justice. It takes ADA complaints.
The Missouri Department of Revenue, the state tax office.
Durable power of attorney. A paper that names someone to act for the person, even if the person loses capacity.
The DHSS division that runs in-home care and DHSS waivers.
pro: DHSS Division of Senior and Disability Services.

plain: The Missouri Department of Social Services. It runs MO HealthNet, FSD, and RSB.
Five kinds of crisis listed in DD rules. They put a person at the top of the wait list, not on a waiver.
Extended period of eligibility. A time after the trial work period when SSDI can restart if pay drops.
The federal Medicaid benefit for people under 21. In Missouri it is called HCY.
pro: Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic and Treatment.

plain: A meeting where a hearing officer reviews an agency's decision. You can bring proof and a helper.
pro: Administrative hearing under 42 CFR 431 Subpart E or agency rules.

plain: Free appropriate public education. The school's duty to a student with an IEP.
Federal benefit rate. The most SSI pays. It is $994 a month in 2026 for one person.
A federal law that keeps school records private. A release lets others see them.
pro: Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act.

plain: Social Security and Medicare taxes taken out of pay.
A device that sends a speaker's voice straight to a hearing aid.
Federal poverty level. Many income limits are a percent of it.
Family Support Division. It decides who gets MO HealthNet, SNAP, and Blind Pension.
Fiscal year. A budget year that does not start in January.
pro: Fiscal year (federal SNAP FY2027 runs 1 Oct 2026 to 30 Sep 2027).

plain: Guardian ad litem. A person the court picks for a short time, for example in an emergency.
A person a court picks to make decisions for an adult who cannot make them, even with help.
pro: Guardian of the person under RSMo Chapter 475.

plain: House Bill and Senate Bill. Names of bills in the Missouri legislature.
Home and community based services. Care at home instead of in a nursing home or institution.
pro: Home and Community Based Services, often via 1915(c) waivers.

plain: Healthy Children and Youth. Extra MO HealthNet services for people under 21. It ends at 21.
A federal law that keeps health records private. A release lets others see them.
pro: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act.

plain: The U.S. housing department. It takes fair housing complaints.
pro: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.

plain: An institution for people with intellectual disabilities. DD waivers need the person to need this level of care.
pro: Intermediate Care Facility for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities (also ICF/DD, ICF/IDD); 42 CFR 435.1010.

plain: Intellectual or developmental disability.
The federal special education law.
pro: Individuals with Disabilities Education Act; 34 CFR Part 300.

plain: Independent educational evaluation. A test by someone outside the school, sometimes at school cost.
Individualized Education Program. A written special education plan for a student.
Independent Living Waiver, a DHSS waiver with a waiting list.
A DDD phone helper for DD-eligible people without MO HealthNet in some counties.
A deal between state agencies to pay for a person's services. These cases can still join a waiver.
pro: Exception named in the DDD wait list memo of 15 Oct 2026.

plain: Individualized Plan for Employment. A written job plan with VR or RSB.
A test score for thinking skills.
pro: Intelligence quotient from an individually administered standardized test.

plain: The U.S. tax agency.
Impairment-related work expenses. Disability costs for work that Social Security subtracts from pay.
In-kind support and maintenance. Free or cheap rent from others that can lower SSI. Food no longer counts.
The yearly service plan made with the support coordinator. Also called the person-centered plan.
pro: Individual Support Plan / Person-Centered Service Plan.

plain: The Lawrence County DD board.
pro: Lawrence County Board for the Developmentally Disabled.

plain: A check of how much care a person needs. Waivers and home care use it.
pro: ICF/IID level of care (DD waivers) or nursing facility level of care (DHSS).

plain: Missouri Adaptive Abilities Scale. The DD test of everyday skills, done by video.
A way of counting income for some MO HealthNet groups.
The state commission that helps Deaf, hard of hearing, and DeafBlind people.
pro: Missouri Commission for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing.

plain: The Missouri Commission on Human Rights. It takes discrimination complaints.
Two kinds of medical doctor.
pro: Doctor of Medicine; Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine.

plain: A code that shows which MO HealthNet group a person is in.
Health coverage for people with low income or disabilities. In Missouri it is called MO HealthNet.
Federal health insurance. It starts after 24 months of SSDI or CDB, or at 65.
pro: Title XVIII; Part A after 24 months of disability entitlement.

plain: The adult nursing waiver for people 21 and older with complex medical needs.
pro: Medically Fragile Adult Waiver, now called Medically Complex Adult Waiver.

plain: MO HealthNet for people who are aged, blind, or disabled.
pro: MO HealthNet for the Aged, Blind, and Disabled.

plain: MO HealthNet Division. It runs Medicaid coverage and payments.
Missouri's name for Medicaid.
Missouri Protection and Advocacy Services. Free legal help with disability rights.
pro: Missouri's federally mandated protection and advocacy system; 1-800-392-8667.

plain: A DD waiver for children under 18 at home. Parents' income does not count. Also called the Lopez waiver.
pro: Missouri Children with Developmental Disabilities (Sarah Jian Lopez) Waiver.

plain: The Missouri Developmental Disabilities Council. It works on system change.
A parent network run by Missouri School for the Blind outreach.
Missouri School for the Blind and Missouri School for the Deaf. Both give free outreach help to age 21.
pro: DESE state schools; outreach birth to 21.

plain: Medicare Savings Program. It can pay the Medicare Part B premium.
Missouri State University in Springfield.
Missouri Vocational Rehabilitation. It helps people with disabilities get and keep jobs.
pro: DESE Office of Adult Learning and Rehabilitation Services, VR.

plain: Occupational therapy and physical therapy.
Can mean prior authorization, which is approval before a service. It can also mean physician assistant.
Plan to Achieve Self-Support. An SSI plan to save money for a work goal.
Private duty nursing. A nurse who gives care in the home for many hours.
Partnership for Hope, a smaller DD waiver paid for partly by county DD boards.
Presumed maximum value. The most that free rent can lower SSI. It is $351.33 in 2026.
Power of attorney. A paper that names someone to act for the person.
Social Security's staff manual.
Priority of Need. A score from 1 to 5 that decides who gets a DD waiver first.
The date of your first contact with Social Security. Benefits can count from that date.
The four Medicare Savings Programs. They pay some Medicare costs for people with low income.
pro: Qualified Medicare Beneficiary; Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary; Qualifying Individual; Qualified Disabled and Working Individual.

plain: The first step to appeal a Social Security decision.
A person Social Security picks to get and manage a person's benefit money.
The federal office that oversees VR agencies.
Rehabilitation Services for the Blind. Free services for people who are blind or have low vision.
pro: DSS FSD Rehabilitation Services for the Blind.

plain: Revised Statutes of Missouri. The book of Missouri laws.
Supplemental Aid to the Blind. Missouri cash that adds to SSI for blind adults.
A county DD board paid for by a local tax. It may fund local DD help.
pro: County developmental disability board, RSMo 205.968 to 205.972 (from Senate Bill 40).

plain: The Stone County DD board.
Standard deviation, a way to measure how far a test score is from average.
pro: Standard deviation; substantial = 2 SD below the mean (9 CSR 45-2.010).

plain: Supported decision-making. The person makes choices with help from people they trust.
A rule that can keep SSI going after the age 18 review. The person must be in an IEP or VR plan.
A federal law against disability discrimination in programs that get federal money.
pro: Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973.

plain: Substantial gainful activity. Pay above $1,690 a month in 2026 can end SSDI or CDB.
Food assistance. Monthly money for food.
Supplemental Nursing Care. A small Missouri grant for people in residential care.
An amount a person must meet each month before MO HealthNet pays, when income is over the limit.
The Social Security Administration.
A Social Security form that shows its disability decision. DDD needs this form.
pro: SSA Disability Determination and Transmittal form.

plain: Social Security Disability Insurance. Pay for disabled workers who paid Social Security taxes.
Supplemental Security Income. Monthly pay for people with disabilities and little income or savings.
Support service provider. A trained helper who guides a DeafBlind person.
pro: MCDHH DeafBlind Support Service Provider program.

plain: A report the school gives when a student leaves with a diploma or ages out.
The DD case manager who makes the service plan and asks for waiver funding.
Southwest Missouri Autism Project. DD money for autism services. No MO HealthNet needed.
Targeted case management, also called support coordination.
Ways to call for people who are Deaf or hard of hearing: text phone or videophone.
pro: Teletypewriter; telecommunications device for the deaf; videophone.

plain: Ticket to Work Health Assurance. MO HealthNet for workers with disabilities, sometimes with a premium.
Trial work period. Nine months when SSDI or CDB continues even with higher pay.
pro: Trial Work Period; 2026 $1,210 a month counts as a service month.

plain: University programs in Missouri that support people with disabilities and families.
pro: University Center for Excellence in Developmental Disabilities; University of Missouri-Kansas City; University of Missouri-St. Louis.

plain: Utilization Review. The DD office review of a service plan and budget.
United States Code. The book of federal laws.
The U.S. agriculture department. It sets SNAP rules and limits.
pro: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Food and Nutrition Service.

plain: Veterans Affairs. Health care for veterans.
Vocational Rehabilitation. Help to get and keep a job.
A one-third cut to SSI when a person lives in someone else's home and gets food and shelter there.
A list of people waiting for a DD waiver. From 15 Oct 2026, new waiver enrollment goes on it.
A Medicaid program that pays for services at home and in the community instead of an institution.
pro: 1915(c) home and community based services waiver.

plain: Work Incentives Planning and Assistance. Free benefits counseling for people on SSI, SSDI, or CDB who work.
pro: SSA-funded WIPA projects; reach through the Ticket to Work Help Line.
